Rashi on Sukkah 33a:10:1.hebrew: עבר ולקטן - לעינבי הדס שהיו מרובין מעלין. ותנן: אם מיעטן — כשר, ואין ממעטין ביו"ט משום שבות, שדומה למתקן כלי ומכשירו; ואם עבר ומיעטן — פסול, כדמפרש טעמא ואזיל:
Rashi on Sukkah 33a:10:1.english: If one transgressed and picked them - [This refers] to the berries of a myrtle branch that were more numerous than its leaves. And we learned [in a Mishnah]: If he reduced them, [the myrtle branch is] fit, but one may not reduce [them] on the Festival due to a rabbinic decree, because it resembles repairing a vessel and making it fit [for use]. And if he transgressed and reduced them, [it is] unfit, as [the Gemara] proceeds to explain the reason.

Rashi on Sukkah 33a:10:2.english: They assumed it - The Rabbis of the study hall, who wished to say that this dispute is over [whether] there is disqualification or there is no disqualification.

Rashi on Sukkah 33a:10:3.hebrew: דכ"ע - רבנן ור' אלעזר בר' צדוק:
Rashi on Sukkah 33a:10:3.english: Everyone - The Rabbis and Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Tzadok.

Rashi on Sukkah 33a:10:4.hebrew: לולב אין צריך אגד - ולא שייך ביה עשיה, דלוקי טעמא דר' אלעזר דפסל משום תעשה ולא מן העשוי בפסולות. וא"נ צריך אגד — אפ"ה משום תעשה ולא מן העשוי לא מיפסיל, דהא בדידיה לא כתיב תעשה:
Rashi on Sukkah 33a:10:4.english: A lulav does not require binding - And [the concept of] an act of making does not apply to it, such that one could attribute the reason of Rabbi Elazar, who disqualifies [it], to “You shall make — and not from that which is [already] made” in [a state of] disqualification. And alternatively, [even if] it requires binding, even so, it is not disqualified on account of “You shall make — and not from that which is [already] made,” for regarding it itself, “You shall make” is not written.

Rashi on Sukkah 33a:10:5.hebrew: ולולב מסוכה לא יליף - הלכך, מהשתא ליכא למיפסליה אלא משום דחוי, דכיון שאגדו בפסול, ונקרא עליו שם לולב של מצוה בשעת דחוי — נדחה לעולם, ואע"ג דלא נראה ונדחה הוא, אלא דחוי מעיקרא. והאי דנקיט פלוגתייהו במיעטן ביום טוב — משום דסתמא בתר דאגדיה הוא, דהא ביום טוב לא אגיד ליה; ואי לא צריך אגד, איצטריך למינקט ביום טוב, משום דאי לאו דקדש היום, אכתי לא חל עליה זמן מצוה ולא שם מצוה למקרייה דחוי:
Rashi on Sukkah 33a:10:5.english: And [a] lulav is not derived from [a] sukka - Therefore, from now on, it cannot be disqualified except on account of rejection, for since he bound it while [it was] unfit, and the designation of a mitzva lulav took effect upon it at a time of rejection, it is rejected forever — even though it is not [a case of having been] fit and [then] rejected, but rather rejection from the outset. And as for the fact that [the baraita] formulates their dispute regarding [one who] reduced them on the Festival — [this is] because ordinarily this is after he has bound it, as on the Festival he would not bind it; and if [a lulav] does not require binding, it was necessary to formulate [the case as occurring] on the Festival, because had the day not become sanctified, the time of the mitzva would not yet have taken effect upon it, nor [would it have] the designation of a mitzva, so as to call it rejected.

Rashi on Sukkah 33a:11:1.hebrew: ומאן דמכשר סבר - אין דחוי לענין מצוה, אלא לענין קדושה, כגון קרבנות:
Rashi on Sukkah 33a:11:1.english: And the one who deems [it] fit holds - There is no disqualification with regard to a mitzvah, but [only] with regard to sanctity, such as sacrificial offerings.

Rashi on Sukkah 33a:12:1.hebrew: לא דכ"ע לא אמרי' יש דחוי במצוה - וטעמא דמאן דפסל משום "תעשה ולא מן העשוי" הוא, דקסבר: לולב צריך למיגד, ושייך ביה עשיה; והכא במילף לולב מסוכה פליגי:
Rashi on Sukkah 33a:12:1.english: No, everyone agrees that we do not say there is disqualification with regard to a mitzvah - And the reason of the one who disqualifies [it] is because of "[You shall] make, and not from that which is [already] made," for he holds [that] a lulav requires binding, and "making" applies to it; and here they disagree about deriving lulav from sukkah.

Rashi on Sukkah 33a:12:2.hebrew: ילפינן - בבנין אב: הואיל וזה בעשיה וזה בעשיה — מה זה ולא מן העשוי, אף זה ולא מן העשוי:
Rashi on Sukkah 33a:12:2.english: We derive - Through a binyan av [general principle]: Since this [one involves] an act of making and that [one involves] an act of making — just as this one [is subject to the rule:] “and not from that which is [already] made,” so too that one [is subject to the rule:] “and not from that which is [already] made.”

Rashi on Sukkah 33a:15:1.english: And I will glorify Him - Beautify yourself before Him.

Rashi on Sukkah 33a:16:2.hebrew: במקום א' - שהענבים כולן ביחד, ומיהו מרובין הן על העלין שבכל ההדס:
Rashi on Sukkah 33a:16:2.english: In one place - That the berries are all together, and nevertheless they are more numerous than the leaves on the entire myrtle [branch].

Rashi on Sukkah 33a:16:3.hebrew: הכי גרסינן - לא שנו אלא במקום אחד, אבל בשנים ושלשה מקומות — כשר. אמר ליה רבא: שנים ושלשה מקומות הוה ליה מנומר, ופסול. הכי גרסינן לה לקמן לענין עלתה חזזית באתרוג:
Rashi on Sukkah 33a:16:3.english: This is our reading - "They taught [this] only in one place, but in two or three places it is fit. Rava said to him: [In] two or three places it is speckled and unfit." So we read it below with regard to [the case of] "A boil arose" on an etrog.

Rashi on Sukkah 33a:1:1.hebrew: אסא מצראה - גדל על המיצר של שדה, ומתוך שיש לו מקום פנוי, הוא משבח ומצליח. לישנא אחרינא: אסא מצראה — הדס מצרי:
Rashi on Sukkah 33a:1:1.english: An Egyptian myrtle - It grows on the border [meitzar] of a field; and since it has open space, it thrives and flourishes. Another version: Asa mitzra’ah — Egyptian myrtle.

Rashi on Sukkah 33a:3:1.hebrew: שלשה בדי עלין לחין - שלשה בדין, ובכל בד ובד שלשה עלין לחין, דבבציר משלשה עלין לא הוי עבות:
Rashi on Sukkah 33a:3:1.english: Three branches of moist leaves - Three branches, and on each and every branch, three moist leaves; for with fewer than three leaves, it is not "plaited."

Rashi on Sukkah 33a:3:2.hebrew: ובראש כל אחד - שיהו עלין הלחין בראשי הבדים, אבל באמצעם — לאו הדר הוא:
Rashi on Sukkah 33a:3:2.english: And at the top of each one - That the moist leaves must be at the tops of the branches, but in their middle — it is not [considered] splendid.

Rashi on Sukkah 33a:4:1.hebrew: ועלתה בו תמרה - כמין תמרה, כעין הנמצא בעלי ערבה — פעמים בעלין דבוק כמין פרי ירוק, וצובעין בו הנשים צעיפיהם:
Rashi on Sukkah 33a:4:1.english: And a berry grew on it - A kind of date, like that which is found on willow leaves — sometimes adhering to the leaves is a sort of green fruit, and women dye their veils with it.

Rashi on Sukkah 33a:5:1.hebrew: ועלתה בו תמרה ביום טוב - משנאגד, דבתלוש נמי סלקא ביה:
Rashi on Sukkah 33a:5:1.english: And a palm shoot grew on it on the Festival - [This refers to a case] after it was bound, for even when detached, [a shoot or leaf growth] can also grow on it:

Rashi on Sukkah 33a:5:2.hebrew: יש דחוי אצל מצות - כלומר, נוהגת תורת דחוי אצל מצות כשם שנוהגת אצל קרבנות — דאם נראה ונדחת משנשחט', אמרת ידחה, דתו לא הדר חזי; הכא נמי, הואיל ונדחה כשנקטם, תו לא הדר מיחזי בעליית תמרה? והשתא לא דייק בין דחוי מעיקרא לנראה ונדחה, דהאי דנקטם מעיו"ט לא נראה מעולם:
Rashi on Sukkah 33a:5:2.english: Is there disqualification with regard to mitzvot - That is to say, does the principle of deferral apply to mitzvot just as it applies to sacrificial offerings — where if [an offering] was fit and then deferred after it was slaughtered, you say it remains deferred, for it cannot revert to being fit; so too here, since [the myrtle branch] was deferred when [its top] was severed, it no longer reverts to being fit with the emergence of a palm shoot [a new tip]? And at this stage, [Rabbi Yirmeya] did not distinguish between an initial deferral and [one that was] fit and then deferred, for this [branch], whose [top] was severed on the eve of the Festival, was never fit [on the Festival].

Rashi on Sukkah 33a:6:1.english: [If] he covered it - A person [covered] the blood of a wild animal or a bird.

Rashi on Sukkah 33a:6:2.hebrew: לא שנו - דכסהו הרוח חייב לכסות, אלא שחזר ונתגלה:
Rashi on Sukkah 33a:6:2.english: They taught - that [if] the wind covered it he is obligated to cover [it], only when it became uncovered again.

Rashi on Sukkah 33a:7:1.hebrew: הואיל ואידחי - על ידי הרוח מכיסוי של מצוה, כדקאמר: דכי לא נתגלה, פטור מלכסות:
Rashi on Sukkah 33a:7:1.english: Since it was set aside - By the wind from the mitzvah of covering, as it states: That if it was not uncovered, he is exempt from covering [it].

Rashi on Sukkah 33a:7:2.english: [It should remain] disqualified - Forever, and even if it became exposed.

Rashi on Sukkah 33a:8:1.english: And Rav Pappa said - [This is what] we read.

Rashi on Sukkah 33a:9:1.hebrew: דרב פפא גופיה - האי דיוקא דרב פפא מיבעיא לי' לר' ירמיה:
Rashi on Sukkah 33a:9:1.english: [That] of Rav Pappa itself - This inference of Rav Pappa was [the subject of] the dilemma for Rabbi Yirmeya.

Rashi on Sukkah 33a:9:2.hebrew: מיפשט פשיט ליה - לתנא דתנא כסהו הרוח חייב לכסות, דאין דחוי:
Rashi on Sukkah 33a:9:2.english: Is it obvious to him - To the Tanna who taught: [If] the wind covered it, he is obligated to cover [it] — that there is no disqualification?

Rashi on Sukkah 33a:9:3.hebrew: לא שנא לחומרא - כי הכא, דמחייב ליה בכיסוי משום טעמא דאין דחוי:
Rashi on Sukkah 33a:9:3.english: There is no difference [whether] to stringency - As [in the case] here, where [the Tanna] obligates him in covering [the blood] due to the reason that there is no disqualification:

Rashi on Sukkah 33a:9:4.hebrew: ולא שנא לקולא - כי ההיא דר' ירמיה, דאי אמרי' אין דחוי — הוי כשר, ואם יש דחוי — הוי פסול, ואמרי' אין דחוי ומכשרינן:
Rashi on Sukkah 33a:9:4.english: And there is no difference [whether] to leniency - Like that [case] of Rabbi Yirmeya, where if we say [that] there is no disqualification, it is fit, and if there is disqualification, it is unfit; and we say [that] there is no disqualification and we deem it fit.

Rashi on Sukkah 33a:9:5.hebrew: או דלמא מספקא ליה - לתנא, ומספיקא לחומרא הוא דמחייב ליה בכיסוי, שמא אין דחוי:
Rashi on Sukkah 33a:9:5.english: Or perhaps it was uncertain to him - To the Tanna; and it is out of doubt, as a stringency, that he obligated him in covering [the blood], lest there is no disqualification.

Rashi on Sukkah 33a:9:6.english: However, for leniency - For example, in the case of the berry.

Rashi on Sukkah 33a:9:7.hebrew: לא אמרינן - אלא פסלינן, שמא יש דחוי או אין דחוי:
Rashi on Sukkah 33a:9:7.english: We do not say - Rather, we invalidate [it, since it is uncertain whether] perhaps there is disqualification or there is no disqualification.

Tosafot on Sukkah 33a:12:1.hebrew: והכא במילף לולב מסוכה קמיפלגי - והוה מצי לאשמועינן פלוגתייהו בליקטן בהיתר, כגון מערב יום טוב לאחר שאגדן. והא דנקט פלוגתייהו בליקטן באיסור, כגון ביו"ט — לאשמועי' דאפילו הכי חכמים מכשירין, דאין דחוי:
Tosafot on Sukkah 33a:12:1.english: "And here, it is with regard to deriving lulav from sukkah that they disagree" - And [the Tanna] could have informed us of their dispute [in a case where] one picked them permissibly, such as on the eve of the Festival after having bound them. And the fact that he formulated their dispute [in a case where] one picked them through a transgression, such as on the Festival — [is] to inform us that even so, the Rabbis deem [it] fit, for there is no disqualification [with regard to mitzvot].

Tosafot on Sukkah 33a:2:1.hebrew: ואימא הכי נמי - תימה: מאי ס"ד למיפסליה משום שם לווי? מידי הדס כתיב בקרא? הא אפי' הירדוף מכשרינן, אי לאו משום דכתיב "דרכיה דרכי נועם":
Tosafot on Sukkah 33a:2:1.english: "And say it is indeed so" - It is puzzling: What could enter [one's] mind to disqualify it because of an accompanying modifier? Is "myrtle" written in the verse at all?! For we would even validate oleander, were it not that it is written: "Her ways are ways of pleasantness" [Proverbs 3:17].

Tosafot on Sukkah 33a:5:1.hebrew: נקטם מערב יו"ט ועלתה בו תמרה ביו"ט מהו - אף על פי שבקונטרס הזכיר נראה ונדחה, הא דהכא דחוי מעיקרא הוא, כיון דבתחלת יו"ט לא חזי, כדמוכח לקמן גבי אשחור מעיו"ט. ונהי דגבי קדשים פשיטא לן דדחוי מעיקרא הוי דחוי — גבי מפריש נקבה לפסחו בפ' מי שהיה טמא (פסחים ד' צח. ושם), וגבי בהמה של שני שותפים בפ"ק דזבחים (ד' יב. ושם) ובפ"ק דקדושין (ד' ז. ושם) — גבי מצוה מיבעיא לן. וכי תימא: הא דאסקינן גבי אשחור תפשוט דדחוי מעיקרא לא הוי דחוי? לא דמיין להכא כדפרישנא לעיל, דשאני התם דבידו ללקט. ואפי' בקדשים מכשירין מה"ט במסכת זבחים פ' כל הפסולין (זבחים דף לד: ושם), דתנן גבי: קבל הכשר ונתן לפסול יחזיר לכשר, ופריך בגמ': וליהוי דחוי! ומשני רב אשי: כל שבידו לא הוי דחוי. ומיהו לא לגמרי דמי להאי דינא, דהא נראה ונדחה הוא, ולקמן מסקינן דלא תפשוט מיני' נראה ונדחה חוזר ונראה, אע"ג דבידו ללקטן; וכן בההיא דהפריש קרבן והמיר דת דבידו לחזור, ואפילו הכי אמרינן פ"ק דזבחים (ד' יב: ושם): הואיל ונדחה ידחה; עוד אמר בזבחים פרק קדשי קדשים (זבחים ד' נט. ושם): כל הקדשים שנשחטו עד שלא נפגם המזבח ואח"כ נפגם המזבח פסולין, דהואיל ונדחה ידחה, אע"פ שבידו לתקן. וצריך לחלק בדברים. והא דמדמי הכא ההיא דכיסוי הדם דבידו לגלות — מכל מקום היה לו לחשבו דחוי, הואיל ונפטר מלכסות לא נתחייב להוציאו מן הדחוי כדי לחזור ולכסות. והא דמייתי: לימא כתנאי, מעבר ולקטן — הוה מצי לדחויי: דמ"ד התם אין דחוי משום דבידו לתקן, אבל הכא דאין בידו לתקן יש דחוי:
Tosafot on Sukkah 33a:5:1.english: "[If] its top was severed on the eve of the Festival and a shoot grew on it on the Festival, what is [the law]?" - Even though in the Kuntres [Rashi] he mentioned [the principle of] "it was fit and then disqualified" [nir’eh venidḥeh], that which is here is [in fact] initial disqualification [diḥui me’ikara], since at the beginning of the Festival it was not fit, as is proven later concerning [berries that] turned black before the Festival. And although regarding consecrated offerings [kodashim] it is obvious to us that initial disqualification is considered a disqualification — in the case of one who designates a female [animal] for his Pesaḥ offering in the chapter [entitled] Mi SheHayah Tamei (Pesachim 98a), and regarding an animal belonging to two partners in the first chapter of Zevachim (12a) and in the first chapter of Kiddushin (7a) — regarding a mitzvah, we have a dilemma. And if you should say: Let that which we conclude concerning [berries that] turned black resolve that initial disqualification is not considered a disqualification? — [these cases] are not comparable to here, as we explained above, for it is different there because it is in his power to pick [them]. And even regarding consecrated offerings they validate on this ground in tractate Zevachim, chapter [entitled] Kol HaPesulin (Zevachim 34b), as we learned regarding: [If] a fit [priest] received [the blood] and gave [it] to an unfit [priest], he should return [it] to a fit [priest]; and the Gemara objects: "And let it be disqualified!" and Rav Ashi resolves: "Anything that is in his power [to rectify] is not [considered] a disqualification." However, [that case] is not completely similar to this law, for behold, it is [a case of] "it was fit and then disqualified," and later we conclude that you cannot resolve from it [the question of whether an object that was] fit and then disqualified can revert and become fit again [ḥozer venir’eh], even though it is in his power to pick them. And similarly, in that [case] where one designated a sacrifice and apostatized, where it is in his power to repent, and even so we say in the first chapter of Zevachim (12b): "Since it was disqualified, it remains disqualified." Furthermore, [the Gemara] says in Zevachim, chapter [entitled] Kodshei Kodashim (Zevachim 59a): All consecrated offerings that were slaughtered before the altar became damaged, and afterwards the altar became damaged, are disqualified, for "since it was disqualified, it remains disqualified," even though it is in his power to repair [the altar]. And one must distinguish among these matters. And as for [the Gemara] comparing here that [case] of covering the blood, where it is in his power to uncover [it]: nevertheless, it should have considered it disqualified, [for] since he was exempt from covering [when the wind covered it], he should not become obligated to remove it from disqualification in order to cover it again. And as for that which [the Gemara] brings: "Shall we say [this dilemma] is subject to a dispute of Tannaim: [If] he transgressed and picked them...?" — [the Gemara] could have rejected [this parallel by arguing] that the one who says there that there is no disqualification [holds so] because it is in his power to rectify [it], but here, where it is not in his power to rectify [it], there is disqualification.
